title: EuIn2Sb2: epitaxially stabilized axion insulator candidate with strong spin-orbit coupling
authors: Hsiang Lee, Shinichi Nishihaya, Markus Kriener, Ayano Nakamura, Tadashi Yoneda, Yuki Deguchi, Makuro Goto, Masaki Uchida
abstract: Eu triangular lattice layer compounds described by the general formula EuA2X2 have attracted growing attention due to a wide range of layered crystal structures and corresponding magnetic topological phases, arising from the coexistence of large Eu magnetic moments and energetically inverted A and X bands. Among the EuA2X2 family, EuIn2Sb2 has been predicted to host robust axion insulator and higher-order topological insulator states by stronger spin-orbit coupling but has not been experimentally realized, including the structural identification. Here we report the epitaxial stabilization of EuIn2Sb2 by adopting the molecular beam epitaxy technique. Structural characterization reveals that EuIn2Sb2 films are based on a unique In-on-In stacking, forming a new trilayer structure distinct from previously predicted structures in the EuA2X2 family. In addition to the in-plane antiferromagnetic ordering at TN=10.5K, the stronger spin-orbit coupling and enhanced In-In hybridization in EuIn2Sb2 make it an ideal candidate of axion insulator and higher-order topological insulator phases. These results establish EuIn2Sb2 as a new member of the EuA2X2 family and offer an advanced platform for exploring these magnetic topological phases.
summary: This work reports the successful epitaxial synthesis of EuIn2Sb2, a material predicted to be a magnetic topological insulator. By characterizing its novel trilayer crystal structure and measuring its magnetic and transport properties, the authors establish it as a promising new platform for investigating axion and higher-order topological insulating phases.
main_problem: To experimentally realize and characterize EuIn2Sb2, a predicted axion insulator and higher-order topological insulator candidate within the EuA2X2 family.
main_result: The authors successfully stabilized EuIn2Sb2 films via MBE, revealing a novel trilayer structure with an In-on-In stacking configuration, which makes it an ideal platform for studying magnetic topological phases.
method: The study employed epitaxial growth using Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE), followed by structural characterization using XRD/TEM and magnetic/transport measurements using SQUID and four-probe methods.
model_or_system: The physical system is the EuIn2Sb2 thin film, belonging to the EuA2X2 family of magnetic topological insulators. The investigation focuses on how strong spin-orbit coupling and the specific crystal structure stabilize exotic topological states.
key_observables: Longitudinal resistivity (rho_xx) showing a kink at TN=10.5K; magnetic susceptibility (chi); and structural confirmation of the trilayer phase via XRD RSM and TEM.
important_parameters: The magnetic ordering temperature (TN=10.5K) and the strong spin-orbit coupling regime are critical parameters defining the topological nature of the material.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed trilayer structure and the presence of in-plane antiferromagnetic ordering are sufficient to establish the material as a candidate for axion/HOTI phases.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structures of EuA2X2 compounds, the successful growth and characterization of the trilayer EuIn2Sb2 film (using XRD/TEM), and the magnetic phase diagram showing temperature and field dependence of resistivity and magnetization.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the theoretical context of EuA2X2 topological insulators, detailing the MBE growth process to stabilize the novel trilayer EuIn2Sb2 structure, and finally characterizing its magnetic and transport properties to confirm its suitability for topological phase exploration.
why_interesting: The combination of magnetic ordering (antiferromagnetism) and strong spin-orbit coupling in a crystalline solid is central to realizing topological phases, which is a major focus in modern condensed matter theory.
